title: Apply a flexible screen protector while peeling its backing
instruction: Align the protector with the phone. Peel the backing as you smooth the film down with the card. Press the whole screen edge to edge, then lift the card clear.
setup: A 150 × 72 × 12 mm dummy phone sits on the work surface. A 140 × 64 mm backed PET protector starts offset 22 mm lengthwise and 12 mm sideways. The pull sticker stands up at one corner. A 106 mm plastic squeegee rests on its edge in a packaging insert. Both hands start empty.
scoring: First align all four corners within 3 mm. After the first bond, award 0.15 × liner fraction peeled, 0.45 × area bonded and 0.30 × area first pressed within 25 mm of the peel front. Full credit requires all three fractions at 1 and the card lifted at least 15 mm for 0.5 s. Zero bonded area scores zero.
fidelity: The phone is fixed. Both hands physically grasp their tools. Tab motion determines liner travel. Where the loaded card crosses exposed film, a 28 × 8 grid records contact and changes color. This approximates film adhesion and bending. The score measures alignment, coverage and peel-and-press coordination. It does not measure trapped air, dust or adhesive strength.
scores: Scripted demo 1.0 in 420 actions (21 s). Dream-1 0.0 in 465 actions (23.25 s). It moved the card and reached the action limit without bonding the leading edge.
reset_notes: Return the card to its insert and place an unbonded protector on its liner at the documented offset. Start with both hands open.
context: A flexible phone protector can shift before the first edge sticks. One hand peels the liner while the other presses the newly exposed film onto the screen.
